The number of promises that are waiting to run (i.e. their internal `fn` was not called yet).

### limit.clearQueue()

Discard pending promises that are waiting to run.

This might be useful if you want to tear down the queue at the end of your program's lifecycle or discard any function calls referencing an intermediary state of your app.

Note: This does not cancel promises that are already running.

When `rejectOnClear` is enabled, pending promises are rejected with an `AbortError`.
This is recommended if you await the returned promises, for example with `Promise.all`, so pending tasks do not remain unresolved after `clearQueue()`.

### limit.concurrency

Get or set the concurrency limit.

### limitFunction(fn, options) <sup>named export</sup>

Returns a function with limited concurrency.

The returned function manages its own concurrent executions, allowing you to call it multiple times without exceeding the specified concurrency limit.

Ideal for scenarios where you need to control the number of simultaneous executions of a single function, rather than managing concurrency across multiple functions.

`onIdle: () => Promise<void>` was added to p-limit's `LimitFunction` declaration and re-exposed on the `limitFunction` wrapper via `Object.defineProperty(limitedFunction, 'onIdle', {value: limit.onIdle})`. Idleness is defined in index.js as `activeCount === 0 && queue.size === 0`, so reserved slots count as active and a job whose promise never settles keeps `onIdle()` pending. Observed in probes and independent verification: an already-idle call resolves immediately; multiple concurrent waiters all resolve when the limiter becomes idle; a rejected job counts as finished; idleness is checked after `next()` resumes the queue, so a job whose completion enqueues another job is not reported idle prematurely; `clearQueue()` releases `onIdle()` waiters when the queue empties and no jobs are active even under `rejectOnClear: false` (the discarded promises stay unresolved), but not while a job is still active. The independent verification reported the `types` and `behavior` checks passing; the implementing task itself ended with taskOutcome failures (model-error, tool-budget-exceeded) before adding the requested new regression test files and the readme update, so those parts were left unverified in that run.
